intent: A size quiz with a trap in the middle: three area bars that put the Andes and the steppe neighbours far below the winner, the Caspian set to scale against the next-biggest lakes because it is a lake, and the launch pad on the steppe where the space age began — landlocked, and still the road to orbit.
pacing_profile: question read verbatim, three options, 3-s beat, reveal with the number, story beats shaped per episode (brief.md), punchline + short follow
pause_policy: Pause only at the marked ellipses; the beat is real silence (ticks come from quizscore.py).
title: Which is the LARGEST landlocked country?

lines.direction: the question, cold — curiosity comes from the map moving under it
lines.text: Which is the largest landlocked country?

lines.direction: quick, each option its own beat

lines.text: Kazakhstan. Only 8 countries on Earth are bigger, and it has not a single metre of ocean coast.

lines.direction: ease back over the steppe; three area bars rise on 'Mongolia' with Kazakhstan on top, a camp sticker beside them; the Bolivian flag-ball thinks on 'Bolivia'; a no-waves sticker on 'sea' as Kazakhstan pulses
lines.text: Mongolia is a little over half that size. Bolivia, under half. Neither touches the sea.

lines.direction: swing west to the Caspian shore; three lake silhouettes rise to scale on 'Caspian' with the Caspian dwarfing Superior and Victoria; the lake tag plates the shore on 'lake'; a wave sticker on 'ocean' as Kazakhstan pulses
lines.text: The Caspian laps its western shore, but it is a lake, the biggest on Earth, sealed from the ocean.

lines.direction: tighten on the launch site; a rocket sticker on 'space'; the Baikonur pin on 'satellite' with the BAIKONUR card; the Kazakh flag-ball grins on 'steppes' as Kazakhstan pulses; the pin leaves at the end
lines.text: Yet the road to space starts here. The first satellite and the first cosmonaut lifted off from a pad on these steppes.

lines.direction: punchline, then a short follow — the outro visual asks
lines.text: Landlocked, and launching rockets. Follow us.
